grammar.name: Congiuntivo trapassato
grammar.scope: formation (avessi fatto, fossi andato); after past main verbs for prior actions (pensavo che fosse già partito); full sequence of subjunctive tenses as an overview

chapters.a_plot: Spring in the Parco dei Tigli: bocce, kids, the 200-year-old plane tree. Surveyors appear with measuring tapes. Franco thought the park had always been protected.
chapters.b_plot: Chiara returns from Rome to good news: Studio Marchetti has been invited to bid for 'a big local project'. She doesn't know what it is yet.
chapters.arc: Season premiere: the park arc is planted.

grammar.name: Hypothetical sentences, type 3 (unreal past)
grammar.scope: se + congiuntivo trapassato → condizionale passato; regrets and counterfactuals; colloquial imperfetto alternative (se lo sapevo, venivo) recognised

chapters.a_plot: At a public meeting at the Centro civico, Lombarda Sviluppo presents its plan: a shopping centre where the park is. The room explodes. 'Se l'avessimo saputo prima...'
chapters.b_plot: Roberto, now a councillor, learns the council approved a preliminary change to the town plan two years ago, before he was elected.

grammar.name: Mixed hypothetical sentences
grammar.scope: past condition → present consequence (se avessi studiato, ora sarei...); present condition → past consequence; all three types compared

chapters.a_plot: The street holds a crisis meeting at Bar Tigli. Everyone blames everyone: if they'd been more involved, the park would be safe now.
chapters.b_plot: Emma, 17, turns the question on the adults: if they'd voted in the last elections, she says, they wouldn't be here now.
chapters.arc: The neighbourhood organises. Emma's activism begins.

grammar.name: Sequence of tenses with the subjunctive
grammar.scope: main clause present/future → congiuntivo presente/passato; main clause past/conditional → congiuntivo imperfetto/trapassato; vorrei che + imperfetto

chapters.a_plot: The 'Comitato Salviamo il Parco' is born. Roberto wants to be president and Ben wants to run the campaign. Old rivalries return.
chapters.b_plot: Chiara discovers what Marchetti's 'big local project' is: the shopping centre on the park. She tells no one.

grammar.name: The passive with essere
grammar.scope: essere + past participle in all tenses; agent with da; when Italian prefers the passive (news, administration)

chapters.a_plot: The committee meets a lawyer, a friend of Nadia's family. Everything has been approved, signed and stamped. The only way is an appeal to the TAR (administrative court).
chapters.b_plot: Matteo, in the middle of it all, signs a lease for a second bar in Milan without telling Nadia.

title.en: It Must Be Done Right Away

grammar.name: Passive with venire and andare
grammar.scope: venire + participle (simple tenses only, dynamic); andare + participle (obligation: va fatto, vanno compilati); andare + participle with perdere/smarrire (è andato perso)

chapters.a_plot: The appeal must be filed within 60 days. Everything must be done now: documents, signatures, fees. Roberto's love of paperwork finally becomes a superpower.
chapters.b_plot: Leo and Pietro create a 'save the park' video for school, which goes viral in Borgoverde.
chapters.runner: The marca da bollo: Ben's nemesis.

grammar.name: The si passivante
grammar.scope: si + third-person verb agreeing with the subject (si vendono case, si è costruito molto); contrast with impersonal si; in compound tenses

chapters.theme: The housing market, property values, gentrification
chapters.a_plot: Estate agents appear on Via dei Tigli: with the shopping centre, 'houses will be worth more'. Some neighbours are tempted to sell. Ben and Chiara, who still pay their mortgage, have an uncomfortable conversation.
chapters.b_plot: Irina (Ornella's carer) tells Ornella about the town she left in Ukraine and its park. Ornella decides to fight.
chapters.arc: The fight gets complicated: not everyone wants the park.

grammar.name: Impersonal si: advanced
grammar.scope: si with reflexives (ci si), with adjectives (si è stanchi), with compound tenses (si è andati), with modals; si vs uno vs la gente

chapters.a_plot: The street gets organised: banners, stands, a sit-in at the park every Saturday. Lucia teaches protest songs; Samira feeds everyone.
chapters.b_plot: Emma and Tommaso are on opposite sides of a small conflict: Tommaso's band has been hired to play at the developer's promotional event.

grammar.name: Past participle clauses (participio assoluto)
grammar.scope: finita la riunione, letto il verbale, arrivati a casa; agreement; pronouns attached (vistolo); formal and written register

chapters.a_plot: Roberto proposes a motion in the town council to suspend the project. Written out in his meticulous minutes, the session reads like a thriller.
chapters.b_plot: Franco attends his first council meeting ever and gets thrown out for heckling.

grammar.name: Compound gerund and causal gerund
grammar.scope: avendo fatto, essendo arrivato; gerund for cause and time in formal prose; subject coherence

chapters.a_plot: Emma and Tommaso (reconciled over the investigation) research the developer in public records and discover the land was sold by the council at a suspiciously low price.
chapters.b_plot: Chiara, having seen the committee's work, can't sleep. She begins secretly redesigning the project.
chapters.arc: Emma–Tommaso reconciled. Chiara's alternative plan begins.

grammar.name: Past infinitive
grammar.scope: aver fatto, essere andato after dopo, dopo di, credere di, pensare di, ricordarsi di, essere sicuro di; with pronouns (averlo visto)

chapters.a_plot: An environmental scientist from the University of Milan speaks at the Centro civico about heat islands and land consumption. The argument shifts from nostalgia to science.
chapters.b_plot: Leo, after seeing a documentary, becomes a climate activist and lectures the family about the car.
chapters.runner: Franco pretends not to be moved by the science.

grammar.name: The journalistic conditional
grammar.scope: condizionale for unconfirmed reports (il sindaco avrebbe firmato, ci sarebbero dei problemi); secondo, stando a, pare che

chapters.a_plot: *La Voce di Borgoverde*'s headline: 'Studio Marchetti would be designing the shopping centre. Among the architects, a resident of Via dei Tigli.' Chiara's secret is out.
chapters.b_plot: The street's reaction: silence at the bar. Ben learns it from the newspaper.

grammar.name: Nominalisation and formal style
grammar.scope: turning verbs into nouns (costruire → la costruzione; decidere → la decisione); nominal style in documents and petitions; formal vs spoken paraphrase

chapters.a_plot: The committee writes its official petition. Roberto writes it in impenetrable bureaucratic Italian; Emma rewrites it so people understand it. They need both.
chapters.b_plot: Chiara and Ben don't speak. She sleeps at Franco's. Lucia mediates.

grammar.name: Concessive connectors
grammar.scope: nonostante, sebbene, benché, malgrado + subjunctive; eppure, tuttavia, ciononostante, anche se (indicative); per quanto + subjunctive

chapters.a_plot: Chiara explains herself to the street at Bar Tigli: why she said nothing, and what she's secretly doing. Nonostante tutto, some forgive her and some don't.
chapters.b_plot: Franco stands up for his daughter in front of everyone, 'sebbene' he disagrees with her.
chapters.arc: Chiara–street reconciliation begins. Franco defends Chiara.

grammar.name: Causal and consecutive connectors
grammar.scope: poiché, dal momento che, in quanto, giacché; pertanto, quindi, di conseguenza, perciò, cosicché, tanto che; building an argument

chapters.a_plot: The TAR hearing in Milan. The lawyer argues, the developer's lawyer argues back, and the street waits outside with thermoses of coffee.
chapters.b_plot: Nadia finds the second-bar lease on Matteo's desk. 'Dal momento che non me l'hai detto...'
chapters.arc: The hearing. Nadia discovers Matteo's secret.

grammar.name: Conditional connectors
grammar.scope: purché, a patto che, a condizione che, qualora, nel caso in cui, a meno che (non), in caso di; negotiation language

chapters.a_plot: Nadia and Matteo negotiate like two lawyers: the second bar can happen, 'a patto che' Matteo meets her conditions. The conditions are many.
chapters.b_plot: The TAR suspends the project for 90 days, 'a meno che' the council approves an alternative. The committee has three months.

grammar.name: Register: formal, neutral, informal
grammar.scope: shifting register for audience (TV interview vs bar vs committee); lexical pairs (cominciare/iniziare/avviare, dire/affermare/dichiarare); formal syntax vs spoken syntax

chapters.a_plot: A regional TV channel comes to Via dei Tigli. Who speaks? Roberto is too formal, Franco too blunt, Matteo too casual. Ben and Ornella together are perfect.
chapters.b_plot: Emma, off camera, coaches everyone on how to talk to the TV. Tommaso films a behind-the-scenes version for social media.
chapters.runner: Pavarotti the cat appears in every shot.

grammar.name: Persuasion: slogans, imperatives, rhetorical questions
grammar.scope: formal and collective imperatives, infinitive imperatives in signs (non calpestare), rhetorical questions, repetition and tricolon

chapters.a_plot: The big protest march from Via dei Tigli to the town hall: the whole ensemble, 800 people and a megaphone. Ornella leads it in her wheelchair.
chapters.b_plot: Franco gives an unplanned speech from the town hall steps about Anna, the park and his tram. It goes viral.

grammar.name: Advanced relative pronouns
grammar.scope: il cui / la cui / i cui (whose); preposition + il quale; relative clauses in formal writing; onde, laddove recognised

chapters.a_plot: Ornella and Franco reveal the plane tree's history: soldiers were hidden beneath it in 1944. If it's proven, the tree can be protected by law. The search for documents begins.
chapters.b_plot: Irina and Ornella search Gino's old papers and find the proof.
chapters.arc: The history of the tree becomes the legal key.

grammar.name: Causatives with pronouns
grammar.scope: fare/lasciare + infinitive with combined pronouns (glielo faccio fare, me lo lascia vedere, farsi + inf. in compound tenses: me lo sono fatto spiegare)

chapters.a_plot: Chiara presents her secret alternative project to the committee: a public park with a small community centre and market, funded by the region. She needs everyone to do something.
chapters.b_plot: Ben, running the bar alone again during Matteo's Milan preparations, learns to delegate, to Leo.
chapters.arc: Chiara's alternative plan is revealed. Ben–Chiara reconcile.

grammar.name: Advanced pronominal verbs
grammar.scope: prendersela, cavarsela, farla finita, averla con qualcuno, metterci, passarsela, godersela, smetterla, spassarsela; forms in compound tenses

chapters.a_plot: Emma and Tommaso break up. It's mutual and sensible, and it hurts like the end of the world.
chapters.b_plot: Bianca, Leo and Ben each try to console Emma, badly. Lucia gets it right with a dance.

title.en: He's the One Who Said It

grammar.name: Emphasis: cleft sentences and focus
grammar.scope: è ... che / è stato ... a + infinitive; è qui che, è per questo che; fronting and dislocation for emphasis

chapters.a_plot: The mayor claims credit for 'listening to citizens'. Who really saved the park? Everybody claims it was them, and Ornella settles it.
chapters.b_plot: Matteo's second bar inspection fails. Who's to blame? Matteo, for once, says: 'È colpa mia.'

grammar.name: The future in the past
grammar.scope: condizionale passato for a future seen from the past (ha detto che sarebbe venuto; sapevo che avrebbe vinto); contrast with English 'would'

chapters.a_plot: The regional official who promised to attend the final council vote doesn't come. The alternative plan might fail without the region's letter of support.
chapters.b_plot: Franco promised Lucia he'd see a doctor about his breathlessness. He didn't. She finds out.
chapters.arc: Final obstacle. Franco's health planted (it pays off in S7).

grammar.name: Presenting and arguing a proposal
grammar.scope: structuring a presentation (in primo luogo, a tal proposito, ne consegue che, alla luce di); hedging and concession; handling objections

chapters.a_plot: Chiara presents the alternative plan to the town council. Marchetti is in the audience. She resigns from his studio publicly, at the end of her presentation.
chapters.b_plot: The region's letter arrives by email at the last minute, sent to Roberto's spam folder. Leo finds it.

grammar.name: Review: the B2 core
grammar.scope: Consolidation of subjunctive sequence, hypotheticals I–III and mixed, passive forms, si constructions, connectors and register

chapters.a_plot: The council approves the alternative plan. The Festa dei Tigli is held in the saved park, under the plane tree.
chapters.b_plot: Chiara announces she's opening her own studio in Borgoverde: 'Studio Ferri'. Her first client is the town.
chapters.arc: SEASON FINALE: the park is saved; Chiara's own studio.
